tip: Regular -ere verbs form the past participle in -uto: ricevere becomes ricevuto.
lavare washes something; add -si (lavarsi) to wash yourself: abbiamo lavato la macchina.
In the passato prossimo, conoscere means met for the first time: ha conosciuto una ragazza.
In non...ancora (not yet), ancora sits between ho and the participle: non ho ancora finito.
aprire has an irregular past participle: aperto, not 'aprito'.
Regular -ire verbs form the past participle in -ito: dormire becomes dormito.
Use suonare for playing an instrument, while games use giocare: hai suonato la chitarra.
Magari plus the imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish: magari fossi = I wish I were.
Grocery shopping is fare la spesa, singular; fare spese means to go shopping around.

english: We always had lunch at one.
tip: Italian often uses the 24-hour clock: alle tredici = at 1 pm.

english: I used to exercise every afternoon.
tip: Facevo sport covers more than 'was exercising': the imperfetto also carries 'used to exercise' and habitual 'would exercise'.

english: If it weren't raining, we'd go out.
tip: A 'se' clause with the imperfect subjunctive pairs with the conditional: se non piovesse, usciremmo.
suo agrees with the thing owned, not the owner, so it means his or her: il suo compleanno.
With body parts, Italian uses a reflexive plus the article, not a possessive: si è tagliata un dito.
Put fa after a time span to mean ago: molti anni fa = many years ago.
Hanno pulito looks like 'have cleaned', but spoken Italian uses the passato prossimo as the plain everyday past: 'they cleaned'.
A past-tense opener like Pensavo che pushes the subjunctive into its past form: fosse, not sia.
buono shortens to buon before a masculine noun: un buon lavoro.
Decisions are 'taken' in Italian: prendere la decisione = to make the decision.

english: I wish it were already summer.
tip: Wishes take vorrei che plus the past subjunctive: Vorrei che fosse means 'I wish it were'.

english: If I were you, I'd accept.
tip: 'se fossi in te' means if I were you, literally if I were in your place.

english: I thought you had already finished.
tip: avessi plus a participle is the past-in-past subjunctive: avessi finito = you had finished.

english: It was very cold that night.
tip: Weather uses fare: faceva freddo = it was cold, literally it made cold.

english: I woke up late this morning.
tip: Reflexives build the past with essere, and the participle matches the speaker: Mi sono svegliato (m), svegliata (f).

target: Il treno arrivava sempre in ritardo.
tip: Repeated past events take the imperfetto: arrivava sempre = 'always arrived', not the one-off passato prossimo.
Essere forms its own past with itself as the helper: siamo stati = we have been, and stati agrees with the plural subject.
With avere as helper the participle stays fixed: hanno avuto (never 'avuti'), no matter the subject.
Spendere has the irregular participle speso: hanno speso = they spent, not 'spenduto'.
The ending -issimo means very or extremely: gentilissimi = extremely kind, stronger than molto gentili.

english: You used to go out every evening.
tip: The imperfetto describes repeated past habits: uscivi ogni sera = you used to go out every evening.
